summary: Franklin County, MA: a 40-ft steel tower on Lighthouse Hill, first operated 1912 and staffed until 1913; the town was flooded for the Quabbin Reservoir and the site is on dry land.

facts.status_note: Brief lists the tower as gone; the register describes only the former site, which it says is still on dry land

events.note: Town of Prescott disincorporated April 28, 1938 as part of the Quabbin Reservoir project

evidence.supports: 40-foot steel tower first operated April 1, 1912 and staffed until 1913
evidence.quote: The 40' steel tower was first operated on April 1, 1912 and was staffed until 1913.

evidence.supports: former site is still on dry land although much of the town is under the reservoir
evidence.quote: Although much of the town is under the Quabbin Reservoir, the former site of this tower is still on dry land.

evidence.supports: town disincorporated April 28, 1938 as part of the creation of the Quabbin Reservoir
town was in Hampshire County before 1938
evidence.quote: Prescott was a town in Hampshire County

evidence.supports: New Salem portion, still above water, is in Franklin County
evidence.quote: the New Salem portion is in Franklin County

evidence.supports: least populous of the four towns, with barely 300 residents by 1900
the New Salem portion is still above water and is known as the Prescott Peninsula
evidence.quote: The majority of the former town (the New Salem portion) is still above water, and is known as the Prescott Peninsula.

evidence.supports: public may not go onto the peninsula except an annual Historical Society tour or hikes run by the Society
evidence.quote: The public is not allowed on the peninsula except for an annual tour given by the Swift River Valley Historical Society

evidence.supports: flooding of four towns for the reservoir, Prescott among them
evidence.quote: it involved flooding four towns in the Swift River Valley

evidence.supports: Prescott disincorporated on April 28, 1938 with Enfield, Greenwich and Dana
evidence.quote: On April 28, 1938, the towns of Enfield, Greenwich, Dana, and Prescott were disincorporated.

evidence.supports: the Quabbin Lookout Tower is a separate 1940 structure on Quabbin Hill Road
evidence.quote: In 1940, the Quabbin Lookout Tower was built on Quabbin Hill Road

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives Franklin County for the site. Wikipedia says the town was in Hampshire County before 1938 and that its New Salem portion, most of which is now above water, is in Franklin County. We could not confirm whether the tower site lies in that portion. The record keeps Franklin.

notes_for_editor: Only the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry describes the tower itself; Wikipedia and the Quabbin history blog cover the town and reservoir. No NHLR entry, visit report or photo found. Wikipedia says the Prescott Peninsula is closed to the public except for Society tours and hikes; whether the tower site is on the peninsula is unconfirmed, so no access fact is recorded. The 1940 Quabbin Lookout Tower is a different structure and should not be merged with this record.
